text: True or False: In the simply typed lambda calculus, every well-typed term is strongly normalizing — every reduction sequence terminates.
explanation: True — strong normalization holds for STLC: every well-typed term reduces to a normal form and no reduction sequence is infinite. This is exactly why non-terminating terms such as Ω = (λx. x x)(λx. x x) and the Y combinator are untypable in STLC, at the cost of Turing-completeness.
